subject: Science
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

questions.title: Weak ciliary muscles: which defect?
questions.text: The vision defect which arises due to gradual weakening of the ciliary muscles and diminishing flexibility of the eye lens is:
steps: ① Ciliary muscles change the lens shape (accommodation)
② With age they weaken; the lens gets less flexible
③ Power of accommodation falls ⟹ near point recedes
④ This age-related defect is presbyopia
∴ Presbyopia → (c)
questions.remember: Presbyopia: old age, weak ciliary muscles, stiff lens; near point moves away. Often both myopia and hypermetropia ⟹ bifocal lenses.
questions.trap: Picking 'both': that describes people who NEED bifocals, but the defect caused by weak ciliary muscles is presbyopia.
questions.tryit: What kind of lens does a bifocal have on its lower part?

questions.title: A shortened eyeball needs which lens?
questions.text: To restore clear vision in persons whose size of the eyeball has reduced, he/she is suggested to use a suitable:
steps: ① Shorter eyeball ⟹ image of a near object forms BEHIND the retina
② That is hypermetropia (far-sightedness)
③ The eye needs extra converging power
④ A convex (converging) lens brings the image onto the retina
∴ Converging lens → (a)
questions.remember: Hypermetropia (short eyeball or long focal length): image behind the retina ⟹ convex lens. Myopia (long eyeball or too-curved lens): image in front ⟹ concave lens.
questions.trap: Picking diverging: that spreads rays out and pushes the image even further behind the retina.
questions.tryit: Is the power of this corrective lens positive or negative?

questions.title: Accommodation and its range
questions.text:
(i) How does the change in curvature of the eye lens help us see nearby objects clearly?
(ii) State the range of the power of accommodation of a normal human eye.
steps: ① Near object: ciliary muscles CONTRACT
② Lens becomes thicker (more curved) ⟹ focal length decreases
③ Image still forms on the retina
④ Normal eye sees clearly from 25 cm (near point) to infinity (far point)
∴ Thicker lens for near objects · 25 cm to infinity
questions.ans: (i) Ciliary muscles contract, the lens becomes thicker, its focal length decreases, so near objects focus on the retina · (ii) 25 cm (near point) to infinity (far point)
questions.remember: Accommodation: the eye lens changes its focal length using the ciliary muscles. Distant objects: lens thin (muscles relaxed). Near objects: lens thick.
questions.trap: Saying the lens moves closer to the retina. In the eye, the lens changes SHAPE, not position.
questions.ncert: NCERT Ch 10 · Section 10.1.1 Power of accommodation
questions.tryit: What is the near point of a normal adult eye?

questions.title: Why a concave lens fixes myopia
questions.text: Why is a concave lens used as a corrective lens for a myopic eye?
steps: ① Myopia: distant objects look blurred
② The image forms IN FRONT of the retina
③ A concave (diverging) lens spreads the rays slightly
④ So they meet farther back: exactly on the retina
∴ Diverging lens of suitable power shifts the image onto the retina
questions.ans: In myopia the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina; a concave (diverging) lens of suitable power diverges the rays so the image forms on the retina
questions.remember: Myopia causes: eyeball elongated, or excessive curvature of the eye lens. Correction: concave lens (negative power).
questions.trap: Writing only 'it diverges light'. Say WHERE the image moves: from in front of the retina onto it.
questions.tryit: A myopic person's far point is 2 m. What is the power of the corrective lens?

questions.title: The elongated eyeball
questions.text:
A person is suffering from a defect of vision due to the elongation of his/her eyeball.
(a) Write the name of the defect of vision and the other possible cause of this defect.
(b) This defect can be corrected by a suitable lens. Draw the ray diagram for the correction of this defect.
steps: ① (a) Elongated eyeball ⟹ myopia (near-sightedness)
② Other cause: excessive curvature of the eye lens
③ (b) Rays from a distant object meet in front of the retina
④ A concave lens in front of the eye diverges them
⑤ They now focus on the retina: clear vision
∴ Myopia · too-curved lens · concave lens diagram
questions.ans: (a) Myopia; the other cause is excessive curvature of the eye lens · (b) diagram: a concave lens before the eye diverges rays from a distant object so they focus on the retina
questions.remember: Diagram marks: the eye with the retina, parallel rays from a distant object, the concave lens, and the rays meeting ON the retina, with arrows.
questions.trap: Drawing a convex lens. Elongated eyeball = myopia = CONCAVE.
questions.tryit: What happens to the far point of a myopic eye?

questions.title: Through a prism: the angle of deviation
questions.text:
(a) Draw the ray diagram for refraction of light through a glass prism and mark the angle of refraction and the angle of deviation.
(b) When the path of a light ray refracted through a glass prism is reversed, how will the angle of deviation change? Explain.
steps: ① Incident ray bends TOWARDS the normal entering the glass
② Inside: angle of refraction r
③ Emergent ray bends AWAY from the normal leaving the glass
④ Angle of deviation D: between the incident ray (extended) and the emergent ray
⑤ (b) Reverse the path: light retraces it exactly
∴ Angle of deviation stays the SAME
questions.ans: (a) Diagram: incident ray, normal, refracted ray (angle r), emergent ray, and D between the extended incident ray and the emergent ray · (b) the deviation stays the same, since light retraces its path
questions.remember: Light paths are reversible: reverse the emergent ray and it retraces the same path, so the angle of deviation is unchanged.
questions.trap: Forgetting to EXTEND the incident ray to mark D: D is between the extended incident ray and the emergent ray.
questions.tryit: Which colour deviates the most in a prism?

questions.title: Scattering vs reflection
questions.text: What is scattering of light? How is scattering of light different from reflection of light? Explain.
steps: ① Scattering: light hits tiny particles and spreads in ALL directions
② It depends on particle size and wavelength (fine particles scatter blue most)
③ Reflection: light bounces off a smooth surface
④ It follows the laws of reflection: angle i = angle r, in one definite direction
∴ Scattering: all directions, by particles · reflection: one direction, by a surface
questions.ans: Scattering: light striking tiny particles is spread in all directions (depends on particle size and wavelength) · Reflection: light bounces off a surface in one definite direction obeying the laws of reflection
questions.remember: The sky looks blue because air molecules scatter blue light most; the sun looks red at sunrise and sunset because blue is scattered away over the long path.
questions.trap: Calling scattering 'reflection in many directions'. Scattering is by tiny PARTICLES and depends on wavelength; reflection is by a SURFACE.
questions.ncert: NCERT Ch 10 · Section 10.6 Scattering of light
questions.tryit: Why does the sky look dark to an astronaut in space?
questions.tryans: There's no atmosphere to scatter sunlight
